sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: What three driving abilities does alcohol degrade — and which three main factors determine blood alcohol concentration?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Alcohol harms clear thinking and physical coordination and slows reaction time, and blood alcohol concentration depends mainly on how much is drunk, how fast and the person's body weight.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Because prescription, over-the-counter, and recreational drugs impair coordination, what two checks belong before driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Many prescription, over-the-counter and recreational drugs impair reasoning and coordination, so check the label and ask a physician or pharmacist about side effects before driving.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Which turn, lane, speed, braking, and night-headlight behaviors flag a possibly impaired driver ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Signs of a possibly impaired driver include wide turns, straddling the center line or weaving, unusual speed, near misses, stopping for no reason, and driving at night without headlights.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: What drifting, following-distance, turning, and turn-signal habits also point to an impaired driver?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: Other warning signs of an impaired driver include swerving or drifting, following too closely, abrupt or illegal turns and inconsistent signaling.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What two immediate steps come first during a roadside breakdown or emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: In a roadside emergency, pull onto the shoulder if you can and turn on your hazard lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: How many feet behind your disabled vehicle should a red reflective triangle sit on straight roads versus hills or curves?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Place a red emergency reflective triangle two hundred feet behind your vehicle, or five hundred feet behind it on a hill or curve.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Through which side should you exit a disabled car on a highway shoulder — after checking what three hazards?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: If you have to get out on a roadside shoulder, exit on the passenger side after checking for traffic, obstructions and drop-offs.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Are all of the Indiana manual's roadside emergency tips mandatory state statutes?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: The manual's roadside emergency tips are safety guidelines that are not necessarily required by Indiana law.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Which three visibility items belong in your vehicle — and where specifically should the flashlight stay?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Keep a flashlight with fresh batteries within the driver's reach, plus a reflective safety vest and a red reflective triangle in the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: Which three cold-weather items should you pack in winter in case you wait hours for a tow?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: In winter, pack blankets, extra gloves and warm hats in case you must wait for responders or a tow.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: Walk through your wheel grip, gas pedal, and exact braking timing during a sudden tire blowout?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: In a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, keep going straight, take your foot off the gas without braking, and brake only when the car is almost stopped off the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What two immediate steps can slow your car and rebuild hydraulic pressure if conventional brakes fail?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: If conventional brakes fail, move to a lower gear when you can, then press the brake pedal hard and fast a few times to build up pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Contrast what your right foot does with the brake pedal in a blowout versus conventional brake failure?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: In a blowout you avoid the brakes until the car is nearly stopped, while in brake failure you pump the pedal hard to build pressure.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: How must your hand work the parking-brake release during brake failure — and what follows once stopped?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: When using the parking brake after a brake failure, hold the release so you can let go if the rear wheels lock, and once stopped, call for help rather than driving on.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: Why must you never turn the ignition to LOCK while rolling in a vehicle with a steering interlock?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while moving in a car with a steering wheel interlock, because the steering will lock and you will lose control.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Should you try switching off your vehicle while it is still rolling during a highway emergency?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Do not try to switch off the vehicle while it is still moving in a highway emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Which five habits — covering keys, doors, spares, idling, and parking spots — cut vehicle theft?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: To reduce theft, take the keys, lock the doors, never hide a spare key in or near the car, never leave it running unattended, and park in well-lit, patrolled areas.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: How should you angle your front tires and set your brake when parking to deter vehicle theft?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: Parking with the front wheels turned sharply right and the emergency brake set helps prevent theft, as can an anti-theft device.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How do you immediately show a police officer behind you that you see their emergency lights?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: When police signal you to stop, turn on your right turn signal to show you have seen the officer.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: What two assumptions might an officer make if you fail to signal when being pulled over?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: If you do not turn on your signal when an officer pulls you over, the officer may think you are avoiding the stop or are impaired.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: Where must you pull over for police — which two spots are off-limits — and what if no safe shoulder exists?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Pull over to the right shoulder, never into the center median or the opposite side of a two-lane road, and if there is no safe shoulder slow down with hazards on until you find a safe place.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Where should you aim to stop during a nighttime pull-over — and what cabin switch helps reassure the officer?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: If stopped at night, look for a well-lit place such as near street lights, restaurants or service stations, and consider turning on the interior light.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: Once stopped for an officer, what three rules govern staying seated, phone calls, and the radio?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: During a traffic stop, stay inside the vehicle unless the officer tells you to get out, end phone calls and turn off the radio.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: If your car has tinted windows, what should you do right after stopping and before the officer walks up?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: If your windows are tinted, roll them all down after stopping and before the officer reaches you.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: Where should driver and passenger hands rest during a stop — and how do you retrieve documents?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: During a traffic stop, keep hands in view, the driver's on the steering wheel and passengers' on their laps, and tell the officer where documents are before reaching for them.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: Does signing a traffic ticket admit guilt — and where does contesting a ticket belong?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Signing a traffic ticket is not an admission of guilt, only an acknowledgment that you received it, and any dispute belongs in traffic court rather than at the roadside.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: What happens to driving privileges if a suspected drunk driver refuses breath, blood, urine, or performance tests?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: A driver suspected of drunk driving who refuses breath, urine, blood or performance tests can lose driving privileges.

sec09-card-sec09-R20.front: What identification must officers provide on request — and which three channels handle misconduct reports?
sec09-card-sec09-R20.expected_back: Officers must give their names and badge numbers on request, and misconduct can be reported to their superiors, internal affairs or a civilian complaint board.

sec09-card-sec09-R21.front: What must Indiana police legally record at every single traffic stop?
sec09-card-sec09-R21.expected_back: Police are legally required to document every traffic stop, including the driver's name and address.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: Why can't your senses detect carbon monoxide — and under what three conditions does it sneak inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Carbon monoxide cannot be seen, smelled or tasted, and it is most likely to enter a vehicle when the heater is on, the exhaust system is faulty, or in heavy traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What is the garage rule for running engines — and how do you set fresh-air vents in traffic versus winter highways?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: Never run a vehicle's engine in a closed garage, and close the fresh-air vent in congested traffic but open it on highways in cold weather.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Contrast when your cabin's fresh-air vent should stay closed versus opened against carbon monoxide?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: The fresh-air vent should be closed in congested traffic, yet opened when driving on highways in cold weather.

sec09-card-sec09-R22.front: Which four physical warning signs point to carbon monoxide poisoning inside a vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-R22.expected_back: Symptoms of carbon monoxide poisoning can include drowsiness or dizziness, bluish skin or lips, headache and increased sensitivity to light.

sec09-card-sec09-R23.front: Where can a leaky exhaust pipe seep fumes — and what maintenance habit and sound clue guard against it?
sec09-card-sec09-R23.expected_back: A faulty exhaust can leak fumes into the back seat, so have the exhaust checked regularly and listen for any unusual roar under the car.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Which three credential categories are issued by the Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: The Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles issues three kinds of credentials: identification cards, learner's permits and driver's licenses.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Which specific credentials sit inside Indiana's permit group versus its license group?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: The learner's permit category covers the driver, motorcycle and commercial learner's permits, while the license category covers the driver's license and the CDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Which Indiana residents qualify to receive a state identification card free of charge?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: An identification card costs nothing for a person who is already eighteen or will turn eighteen on or before the next General or Municipal Election.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What card orientation and two milestone dates appear on Indiana credentials issued under age twenty-one?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: Credentials for Indiana residents under twenty-one use a vertical layout and print the dates on which the holder turns eighteen and twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: What year did Indiana launch redesigned high-security credentials, and what happens to older cards?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: Indiana began issuing redesigned credentials with new security features in two thousand nineteen, and older cards remain valid until the expiration date printed on them.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: What visual symbol on an Indiana credential shows Real ID compliance for federal identification?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: A star in the upper right corner shows that a credential is Real ID-compliant and can serve as identification for federal purposes.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Why did Congress pass the Real ID Act of two thousand five for state credentials?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: The federal Real ID Act of two thousand five set minimum standards so that compliant state credentials can be used for federal purposes such as boarding commercial flights or entering military and other secure federal sites.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Since what exact date has Indiana satisfied federal Real ID Act standards?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Indiana has met the Real ID Act requirements since January one, two thousand ten.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which state licenses and ID cards will DHS and TSA accept at airport checkpoints and federal buildings?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Federal agencies such as DHS and TSA accept only Real ID-compliant licenses and ID cards for entry to federal facilities, TSA airport checkpoints included.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: During which three transactions can you upgrade to Real ID, and what document formats qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: A non-compliant Indiana credential can be upgraded to Real ID during a renewal, amendment or replacement, using original documents or certified copies.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: Which four proof categories must you bring to a BMV branch for a Real ID upgrade?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: For a Real ID upgrade the branch visit must include documents proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and Indiana residency.

sec01-card-sec01-R18.front: Where can applicants review the complete Real ID document list or call the BMV toll-free?
sec01-card-sec01-R18.expected_back: The full Real ID document list is in Appendix A and at REALID.IN.gov, and the BMV toll-free line is eight hundred eighty-eight-six hundred ninety-two-six thousand eight hundred forty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Who may get an Indiana credential, and what three ties demonstrate legal state residency?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.memory_hook: Sole home, voter roll, school-age kid
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Only legal Indiana residents can obtain an Indiana credential; residency can be shown by keeping an Indiana home address without claiming another state, by being registered to vote in Indiana, or by having a dependent enrolled in an Indiana elementary or secondary school.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: Which four groups staying in Indiana are excluded from resident status for BMV credentials?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: For credential purposes, college students and active-duty service members who do not claim Indiana residency, temporary employees and anyone not intending Indiana to be a permanent home are not treated as residents.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: What happens before Indiana processes your application if you hold a card from another state or territory?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: If the BMV finds that an applicant already holds a credential from another state, territory, DC or Puerto Rico, that card must be surrendered before the Indiana application is processed.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How many driver or ID credentials may an Indiana resident hold at once across all states?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Indiana residents may hold only one credential at a time, even when the other one came from another state, so any other credential is surrendered when applying.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: Within how many days of becoming an Indiana resident must a licensed newcomer get an Indiana license?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: A person who becomes an Indiana resident has sixty days to get an Indiana driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: How long must a new Indiana resident who never held another state's license hold a learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: A new resident who has never held a valid license from another state must hold an Indiana learner's permit for one hundred eighty days before applying for a driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How do Indiana's sixty-day and hundred-eighty-day clocks split for new residents?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The sixty-day deadline applies to a new resident getting an Indiana license, while the one hundred eighty-day rule applies to holding an Indiana learner's permit when the person was never licensed in another state.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Which three alternative items let a new resident eighteen or older transfer a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: A new resident aged eighteen or older with a valid out-of-state license brings one of three items: that license, a copy of the official driving record, or a verification letter.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Which two out-of-state license conditions trigger taking Indiana's knowledge exam upon transfer?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.memory_hook: Expired under five, held under year
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: A knowledge exam is required when the out-of-state license expired less than five years ago or has been held unrevoked for less than one year.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: Which exams are required if an applicant's out-of-state license expired more than five years ago?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: When the out-of-state license has been expired for more than five years, the applicant must pass both a knowledge exam and a driving skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: How does crossing the five-year expiration mark change transfer testing for an out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.memory_hook: Under five written, over adds drive
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: An out-of-state license expired for less than five years means a knowledge exam only, while one expired for more than five years means a knowledge exam plus a driving skills test.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: What age, prior license tenure, and branch screenings apply to a transferring driver under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A transferring applicant under eighteen must be older than sixteen years and one hundred eighty days and have held a valid out-of-state license for at least one hundred eighty days, and must also pass a knowledge exam and a vision screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: What age and license rules govern who can receive an Indiana identification card?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: An identification card can be issued to an Indiana resident of any age who does not hold a driver's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: How can an Indiana ID cardholder qualify to ride a motor driven cycle?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: An ID card holder aged at least fifteen who passes an MDC knowledge exam receives an MDC endorsement on the card and may operate a motor driven cycle.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: How long do an Indiana ID card and MDC endorsement last, and what changes for temporary residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: An identification card and an MDC endorsement are valid for six years, but cards for lawful temporary residents expire on the end-of-stay date.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What documents and branch checks earn a learner's permit once an applicant reaches sixteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: An applicant aged sixteen or older gets a learner's permit by proving identity, lawful status, Social Security number and residency with Appendix A documents and passing a vision screening and a knowledge exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What minimum age, form, and three-week timing rule apply to getting a learner's permit before sixteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.memory_hook: Fifteen, CDE form within three weeks
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: An applicant under sixteen must be at least fifteen and show a Certificate of Driver Education Enrollment from a BMV-licensed behind-the-wheel provider, dated no more than three weeks before the class starts.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: What extra hurdles apply to a fifteen-year-old permit applicant compared with someone sixteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: A learner's permit applicant aged sixteen or older needs documents, a vision screening and a knowledge exam, while one under sixteen must also be at least fifteen and show proof of enrollment in behind-the-wheel training.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Can an online theoretical course completion certificate serve as proof of driver-education enrollment at the BMV?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: The certificate of completion from an online theoretical course is not accepted as proof of driver education enrollment.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What emergency-contact rule applies to a learner's permit applicant younger than eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A learner's permit applicant younger than eighteen must name an emergency contact who is at least eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: How long does an Indiana learner's permit stay valid, and what exception applies to temporary residents?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Learner's permits are valid for two years from the issue date, except that permits for lawful temporary residents end on the end-of-stay date.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: How does the lifespan of an Indiana ID card or MDC endorsement compare with a learner's permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: An identification card and an MDC endorsement both last six years, while a learner's permit lasts two years from issue.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: When does renewing an expired Indiana learner's permit require retesting?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Renewing a learner's permit that has been expired for more than one hundred eighty days requires retesting.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: After retaking the knowledge exam for a long-expired permit, does your earlier valid permit time still count?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The knowledge exam is retaken after a permit has been expired for more than one hundred eighty days, and any time spent holding a valid permit still counts toward the one hundred eighty-day holding period.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: Before turning sixteen or finishing driver-ed, who may supervise a fifteen-year-old enrolled permit holder?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A permit holder under sixteen who is enrolled in driver education may drive with a licensed driver training instructor or a BMV-recognized certified driver rehabilitation specialist sitting in the front passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Which family members or spouses in the front seat may supervise a permit holder under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: A permit holder under eighteen may practice with a relative by blood, marriage or legal status who is at least twenty-five and holds valid driving privileges, or with a licensed spouse who is at least twenty-one, seated in the front passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Who may supervise practice driving once a learner's permit holder is eighteen or older?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: A permit holder aged eighteen or older may practice only with a validly licensed driver who is at least twenty-five, or with a licensed spouse who is at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does Indiana's minimum age for a supervising relative compare with a supervising spouse?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: A relative supervising permit practice must be at least twenty-five, but a spouse supervising permit practice need only be licensed and at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Who may supervise driving practice for a minor permit holder under Department of Child Services care?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A permit holder under eighteen who is in the care of the Department of Child Services may practice with a licensed relative aged at least twenty-five or with a licensed driver aged at least twenty-five whom the Department approves.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: If a minor permit holder is not enrolled in driver education, which professionals may still supervise up front?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A permit holder under eighteen who is not in driver education may also drive with a licensed driver training school instructor working for a school, or a BMV-recognized certified driver rehabilitation specialist, in the front passenger seat.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Who takes a BMV vision screening, and what must glasses or contact-lens wearers do?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Every permit or license applicant, renewals included, must pass a vision screening unless eligible to renew online, and drivers who wear glasses or contacts should say so and wear them for the screening.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: What happens after failing a branch vision screen, even when you bring back a doctor's letter?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Failing the branch vision screening can lead to further evaluation, and Driver Ability may still require more testing even when the customer brings a doctor's letter.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: What three sources feed Indiana's multiple-choice knowledge exam, and what signs must you understand?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: The knowledge exam is a multiple-choice test drawn from Indiana law, defensive driving practices and this manual, and it expects you to read and understand regulatory, warning and traffic signs and signals.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: Which four applicant groups must pass Indiana's driver knowledge exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: The knowledge exam is required for permit applicants, new residents whose out-of-state license is expired or who hold a valid out-of-country license, new residents under eighteen with an out-of-state license, and residents whose Indiana license expired more than one hundred eighty days ago.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: How many active points on your Indiana driving record trigger a mandatory knowledge exam at renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: A driver renewing a license with six or more active points on the Indiana record must also take the knowledge exam.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: When must returning active-duty military personnel or dependents take the knowledge exam to renew?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Active-duty military members, spouses or dependents whose Indiana license has been expired more than one hundred eighty days and who returned from service outside Indiana more than ninety days before renewal must take the knowledge exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: How early before branch closing must you arrive for a knowledge exam, and when can you retry?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.memory_hook: Thirty minutes early, retry next business
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: To take the computer-based knowledge exam the same day you must arrive at least thirty minutes before the branch closes, and after a failure you must wait until the next business day to retake it.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: Beyond standard passenger driving, which four specialty operations have BMV knowledge exams?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Besides the driver's knowledge exam, the BMV offers knowledge exams for CDL endorsements and for motorcycle, MDC and for-hire operation.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: What course hours let a permit holder take the skills exam at a participating school, and how long does it count?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: A permit holder can take the driving skills exam at a participating BMV-licensed driver training school after finishing a course of thirty hours of theory and six hours behind the wheel, and that result stays valid until the permit expires.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: Does an Indiana learner's permit need restriction J for a driver training school to administer your skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: Driver training schools may give the skills exam to any holder of a valid Indiana learner's permit, whether or not the permit carries driver's education restriction J.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What two driver-education situations force a student to take the skills exam at a BMV branch instead?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: The skills exam must be taken at a BMV branch instead if the student fails either part of the driver education course or the school does not take part in the skills test program.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Which two newcomer groups must take their driving skills exam specifically with a BMV examiner?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: A BMV examiner must give the skills exam to new residents under eighteen who held an unrevoked out-of-state license for at least one hundred eighty days but less than one year, and to new residents holding an out-of-country license.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: Which three expiry, restriction, or medical situations also require a BMV skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: A BMV skills exam is also required when an Indiana license has been expired more than five years, when a BMV restriction requires testing, or when a medical complaint or the medical board leads the BMV to require an evaluation.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: What booking window, vehicle rule, and BMV fee apply to scheduling a branch driving skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.memory_hook: Forty-eight hours to three weeks, free
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: A BMV driving skills exam can be booked no more than three weeks and no less than forty-eight business hours in advance, the applicant supplies the vehicle, and the BMV charges nothing for it.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: Who is allowed inside the vehicle with you during a BMV driving skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: Only the BMV examiner or other authorized BMV staff may ride in the vehicle during the driving skills exam.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How are interior cabin cameras and factory backup cameras treated during the driving skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: Interior cameras must be switched off for the whole skills exam, though backup cameras are allowed.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: What five condition and paperwork standards must your vehicle meet before starting the skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: The test vehicle must be legally equipped, insured, safe and clean, and its current registration must be shown before the exam.

sec01-card-sec01-F43.front: Which equipment or registration defects can make an examiner reject your test vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F43.memory_hook: Bad registration, tires, bumper, glass, doors
sec01-card-sec01-F43.expected_back: The examiner may reject a vehicle, for example one that is not properly registered or has unsafe tires, a missing bumper, broken glass or mirrors, or a door that does not work.

sec01-card-sec01-F44.front: Does the BMV examiner coach you during the skills exam, and what happens right before driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F44.expected_back: The examiner does not teach during the exam but scores the drive objectively on a standardized form, after asking a few required questions.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: Which seven core on-road behaviors does the examiner grade during the skills exam?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.memory_hook: Lanes, gaps, passes, speed, defense, stops
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Skills exam scoring covers lane use and signaling, a safe gap to the vehicle ahead, holding speed and leaving room when being passed, speed control, defensive habits, following instructions and approaching intersections with a full stop when required.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: What symbol prints on the front of your Indiana credential when you register as an organ donor?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: Choosing to be an organ donor puts a small heart on the front of your credential.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: Once someone eighteen or older registers as an organ donor in Indiana, can relatives override that decision at death?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Under Indiana's Donor Choice Law, a person aged eighteen or older can declare the wish to be an organ donor, and family members cannot override that choice at death.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What two stages of parent or guardian approval apply when someone under eighteen wants to be an organ donor?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: A person under eighteen can declare the wish to donate only with a parent's or legal guardian's permission, and that adult must consent to donation when the minor dies.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Contrast family authority at death for an adult organ donor versus a donor under eighteen?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: An adult's donor declaration cannot be overridden by family, while a minor's declaration depends on a parent or guardian consenting at the time of death.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What military ID must an active-duty U.S. service member show at a BMV branch to add an active-duty indicator?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces can add an active-duty indicator by showing a current Common Access Card (CAC) at a branch during a new issuance or renewal.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: Which discharge condition and Defense Department form let a veteran add an Indiana veteran indicator?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: A veteran who was not dishonorably discharged can add a veteran indicator by providing a Department of Defense DD two hundred fourteen that verifies the discharge.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: Which three documents must a deceased veteran's surviving spouse bring to add a veteran spouse indicator?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: A surviving spouse of a deceased veteran can add a veteran spouse indicator by presenting proof of the veteran's discharge or separation, the marriage certificate and the veteran's death certificate.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Match the active-duty, veteran, and veteran-spouse indicators to the exact paperwork backing each one?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: An active-duty indicator is backed by a current Common Access Card, a veteran indicator by a DD two hundred fourteen, and a veteran spouse indicator by discharge proof plus marriage and death certificates.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: Above what engine horsepower must a watercraft operator generally carry a valid driver's license in Indiana?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Anyone operating a watercraft whose engine produces more than ten horsepower must carry a valid driver's license.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: How can an unlicensed person aged fifteen or older legally run a boat over ten horsepower?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: A person aged fifteen or older without a driver's license may operate such a watercraft only after finishing a boater education course that the Indiana Department of Natural Resources has approved, and must carry a valid Indiana ID card while doing so.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Can someone under fifteen ever operate a watercraft with an engine exceeding ten horsepower in Indiana?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Nobody younger than fifteen may operate a watercraft with an engine of more than ten horsepower.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: Contrast Indiana's over-ten-horsepower boating rule for unlicensed teens fifteen-plus versus kids under fifteen?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: Unlicensed operators aged fifteen or older may run a watercraft exceeding ten horsepower only after completing an approved boater education course and while carrying a valid Indiana identification card, whereas anyone under fifteen is barred from operating one.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: How does a suspended driver's license affect boating — and how do reckless or intoxicated boat violations hit your record?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: A person whose driver's license is suspended may not operate a watercraft, and reckless or intoxicated boating or breaking watercraft laws can add points to the driver record.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: On Indiana boundary waters, when must Hoosiers carry an Indiana license versus out-of-state boaters?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: On Indiana boundary waters, Indiana residents operating a watercraft must carry an Indiana driver's license, while residents of other states need one only on an embayment, river or stream in Indiana.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Contrast the Indiana driver's license rule on boundary waters for Indiana residents against out-of-state residents?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Indiana residents on boundary waters must carry an Indiana license, while out-of-state residents need one only on an Indiana embayment, river or stream.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: Which three groups of individuals or organizations qualify for an Indiana disability parking placard?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: A disability parking placard is available to people with a permanent or temporary disability, to people issued or eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate, and to organizations providing transportation or facilities for people with physical disabilities.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: What kind of company may apply for an organizational disability parking placard?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: A company empowered by the state or a political subdivision to run transportation or facility programs for people with physical disabilities may apply for a placard.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: Which practitioners can sign State Form forty-two thousand seventy for a placard — and how do you submit it?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: To apply, a health care provider (for example a physician, chiropractor, podiatrist, physician's assistant, advanced practice registered nurse, optometrist or ophthalmologist) completes State Form forty-two thousand seventy, which can be taken to any branch or mailed.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: Which applicants never need a health care provider's signature to obtain a disability parking placard?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: No health care provider certification is needed for a person who has received or is eligible for a Disabled Hoosier Veteran plate.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What does an Indiana permanent disability placard cost — and what two certifications could ever end it?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: A permanent placard is free and does not expire unless a provider certifies the disability is no longer permanent or the Indiana Department of Veteran Affairs certifies the holder is no longer a Disabled Hoosier Veteran.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Does a temporary disability placard charge a fee — and which date ends it first?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: A temporary placard carries a fee and expires on the provider's stated date or one year after issue, whichever comes first.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Contrast Indiana's permanent disability placard against its temporary placard on price and duration?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A permanent placard is free and open-ended, while a temporary placard has a fee and lasts at most one year.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: On what calendar date — or earlier operational change — does an organization's disability placard expire?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: A placard issued to an organization expires on January one of the fourth year after the issue year, or earlier if it stops running programs or facilities for people with disabilities.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: What penalty hits expired-placard use — and may a valid placard holder ever park on the diagonal stripes?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Using an expired placard can lead to a fine, and parking in the diagonally striped area beside a reserved space is never allowed, even with a valid placard.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: What temporary option helps an Indiana resident who loses a credential while temporarily living out of state?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: A person who loses a credential while temporarily living outside Indiana may be able to get an interim credential.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What detail stability unlocks myBMV.com renewal — and how often in a row may you renew online or at a kiosk?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: If your name and residential address have not changed, you may be eligible to renew or replace online at myBMV.com, and online or BMV Connect kiosk renewal is allowed every other renewal.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: At what exact age-plus-days mark does a probationary license expire — versus midnight when for other credentials?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A probationary license expires at twenty-one years and thirty days and may be renewed online if the holder qualifies, while all other credentials expire at midnight on the holder's birthday.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does a probationary license's expiration rule stand apart from standard Indiana licenses and IDs?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: A probationary license ends at twenty-one years and thirty days, whereas every other credential runs out at midnight on the holder's birthday.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: When does your credential actually expire if your birthday lands on a Sunday or holiday when BMV branches are closed?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: If your birthday falls on a day when branches are closed, the credential expires at midnight on the next business day.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: Do credentials held by residents with temporary lawful status follow standard birthday expiration cycles?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: Credential expiration dates differ for residents with temporary lawful status.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What universal charge hits anyone who renews an Indiana credential after its expiration date?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: Everyone who renews a credential after its expiration date is subject to an administrative penalty.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: What three requirements hit when renewing a license expired at least one hundred eighty days up to five years?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: Renewing a license expired for at least one hundred eighty days but not more than five years requires the administrative penalty, a knowledge exam and a standard vision screening.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: What extra behind-the-wheel requirement joins the penalty, written test, and vision check once expired five years or more?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: Renewing a license expired for five years or more requires the administrative penalty plus a knowledge exam, a driving skills exam and a standard vision screening.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: Contrast renewing a license expired one hundred eighty days to five years against one expired five years or longer?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Renewing a driver's license expired from one hundred eighty days up to five years requires an administrative penalty, a knowledge exam, and a standard vision screening, while one expired five years or longer also requires a driving skills exam.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: How early may U.S. citizens and permanent residents renew a license or ID — versus temporary lawful residents?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: US citizens and permanent lawful residents can renew a license or ID card up to twenty-four months before it expires, while people with lawful temporary status can renew only up to thirty days ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: How many days before expiration may you renew an Indiana learner's permit?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: A learner's permit can be renewed up to thirty days before it expires.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Group which Indiana credentials renew twenty-four months early versus which cap at thirty days early?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: A citizen or permanent resident may renew a license or ID card as early as twenty-four months ahead, but a learner's permit or a lawful temporary resident's credential only thirty days ahead.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: At age twenty-one or older, how many active points on your record force a written exam at renewal?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: A driver aged twenty-one or older with six or more active points must pass the knowledge exam to renew the license.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: What driving-record threshold triggers a mandatory knowledge exam at renewal for drivers twenty-one and up?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: The knowledge exam at renewal is triggered by six or more active points for drivers aged twenty-one or older.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: For how many days does an Indiana license stay valid after a service member's out-of-state tour, deployment, or discharge ends?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: A license held by someone serving outside Indiana with the US Armed Forces stays valid for ninety days after discharge, post-deployment or the end of the out-of-state service residence.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: What discharge paperwork lets a returning veteran renew an expired license at a branch — and what bonus can they add?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: To renew an expired license after discharge, a veteran visits a branch with Department of Defense proof of discharge or the long form DD two hundred fourteen, and can add the veteran indicator at that visit.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: To which chapter and topic does the Indiana manual direct chauffeur and public-passenger chauffeur holders for renewal rules?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: For chauffeur and public passenger chauffeur licenses, the manual sends readers to the For-Hire Endorsement section of Chapter two for renewal, amendment and replacement details.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: What must you do with your Indiana credential after legally changing personal information — and where?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: After legally changing personal information you must amend your credential, which can be done at any BMV branch.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: Within how many days — and how — must you report a change of principal legal address and amend your credential?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: A change of principal (legal) address must be reported and an amended credential applied for within thirty days, in person at a branch with Appendix A documents.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: Through which three channels can you update just your mailing address?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: A mailing address can be changed online at myBMV.com, at a BMV Connect kiosk or at a branch.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: Contrast how Indiana handles a principal home-address change versus a mailing-address change?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: A principal address change needs a branch visit with documents within thirty days, while a mailing address change can be done online, at a kiosk or at a branch.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: Walk through the agency order, waiting time, and deadline for amending your credential after a name change?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: For a name change, update Social Security records first, wait at least one business day, then visit a branch within thirty days of the change with Appendix A documents to amend the credential.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: When your Indiana license, permit, or ID is unexpired, how and at what cost can you replace a Social Security card?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: If your Indiana license, permit or ID card is not expired, the manual says the SSA card replacement can be done online at no cost.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: Under what condition can you replace a lost or stolen credential online or at a kiosk — and up to how many times?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: A lost or stolen credential can be replaced through myBMV.com or a BMV Connect kiosk when the name and residential address are unchanged, up to ten online replacements before a branch visit is required.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: What happens once you have already ordered ten online replacements for a credential?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Online replacement is capped at ten times, after which the holder must replace the credential at a BMV branch.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: If your card is lost AND something besides your mailing address changed, why can't you order online — and what must you do?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: If anything other than the mailing address has changed, a replacement cannot be ordered online; the holder must amend the credential at a branch within thirty days with Appendix A documents.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What does a work-zone flashing arrow board tell you when its lights flash without pointing left or right?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.memory_hook: No arrow means caution, hold lane
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: A flashing arrow board that points in neither direction is a caution signal and does not require you to change lanes.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: What must you do when a work-zone flagger extends an orange or red flag straight into your lane, and when may you move?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.memory_hook: Horizontal flag stops; wait for wave
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: You must stop when a flagger holds an orange or red flag straight out into your lane, and you may continue at reduced speed only when the flagger directs you to.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: How must you respond to each side of a work-zone flagger's handheld sign paddle?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.memory_hook: Stop on STOP, creep on SLOW
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: When a flagger uses a sign paddle, stop for the STOP side and proceed slowly for the SLOW side.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: What does zipper merging mean at a lane closure, and why do some work zones post signs for it?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: At some work zones, signs ask drivers to merge late toward the lane closure, known as zipper merging, to shorten the back-up.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Why is speeding into a work zone so risky, and how should you space your car inside one?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Speeding into a work zone means meeting slowed or stopped traffic within seconds, so slow down and keep a safe distance on all sides.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: Which three categories of vehicles must stop fifteen to fifty feet before railroad tracks, and where is that stop waived?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Passenger-for-hire vehicles, all school buses, and vehicles transporting explosives or flammable liquids must stop fifteen to fifty feet from the nearest rail at railroad crossings, except at signed abandoned tracks or crossings where the rails have been removed.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: At which two kinds of railroad crossings does the mandatory stop rule not apply?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.memory_hook: Skip signed abandoned or removed rails
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: The required railroad stop does not apply at abandoned tracks marked with signs or where the tracks across the road have been removed.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Which standard traffic sign does a standalone railroad crossbuck act like, and when must you stop at one?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.memory_hook: Solo crossbuck yields; train means stop
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: A crossbuck by itself works like a yield sign, so the choice to stop is yours, but you must stop if a train is coming.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: What is required when a railroad crossbuck is mounted together with a stop sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: A crossbuck paired with a stop sign requires a complete stop, and you may cross only after making sure no train is approaching.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Once railroad bells, flashing lights, or gates activate, how long must you remain stopped?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.memory_hook: Wait until off or waved through
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: When warning bells, flashing lights or gates are active, stay stopped until the warning ends or a police officer or railroad flagman waves you through.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What does Indiana law say about weaving around a lowered crossing gate or racing an approaching train?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.memory_hook: Never skirt gates or race trains
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Driving around a lowered crossing gate is illegal, and you should never try to race a train to a crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What must you confirm before starting across railroad tracks, and what happens if your vehicle stalls on them?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: Never start across railroad tracks unless you can clear them without stopping, and if your vehicle stalls on the tracks everyone should get out at once.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: About how many seconds do you have to clear a crossing once lights start flashing and gates begin lowering?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: Once crossing lights flash and the gate starts down, you have roughly twenty seconds to get off the crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: If your car is stuck on the tracks and a train is approaching, how should everyone evacuate and whom do you call?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: If you are stuck on the tracks with a train coming, get everyone out and run away from the tracks at a forty-five-degree angle toward the oncoming train, then call nine one one.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: When a vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks with no train in sight, whom should you call first and second?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: If your vehicle is stuck on a crossing and no train is coming, call the Emergency Notification System number on the blue sign at the crossing first, then call nine one one.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: At a crossing with two or more tracks, what must you verify right after one train finishes passing?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Where there is more than one track, after one train clears make sure another train is not coming on the other track or from the opposite direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Within what distance of a railroad crossing are you barred from passing another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: Do not pass another vehicle within one hundred feet of a railroad crossing.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: Where trains share the middle of a city street, how do traffic signals warn drivers of an approaching train?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: Where trains run in the middle of a street, traffic signals flash red in every direction when a train approaches, and drivers treat that like any crossing warning.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: What changes about approaching trains at gated crossings inside designated local quiet zones?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: In local quiet zones, approaching trains do not sound their horns at some gated crossings.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: What trend makes following a school bus toward railroad tracks especially important to anticipate?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: School buses stop at railroad crossings, and rear-end crashes into buses stopped there have increased.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Without a special oversize or overweight permit, what are Indiana's maximum vehicle width, height, and weight?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: Without a special permit, a vehicle may be at most eight feet six inches wide, thirteen feet six inches high and eighty thousand pounds.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, how does a passenger car's stopping distance compare with a loaded tractor-trailer's?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: A car at fifty-five miles per hour can stop in about one hundred thirty to one hundred forty feet, but a fully loaded tractor-trailer with hot brakes can need more than four hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Where are the four blind-spot zones around a tractor-trailer, including the front and rear distances?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: A tractor-trailer's blind spots extend up to twenty feet in front of the cab, along both sides, beside the cab, and up to two hundred feet behind the trailer.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: When trailing behind a tractor-trailer, what rule tells you instantly whether the truck driver can spot your car?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: When following a tractor-trailer, if you cannot see the driver's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: On which side and in what manner should you always pass a tractor-trailer?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: Pass a tractor-trailer completely and always on the left, without lingering beside it.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: Why do tractor-trailer drivers often swing wide before making a tight corner?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: A tractor-trailer's rear wheels track a shorter path than its front wheels, so its driver often swings wide first to make a tight turn.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: When approaching your highway exit near a tractor-trailer, why should you drop behind rather than cut ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Cutting in front of a tractor-trailer to reach an exit removes its safety cushion; slow down and exit behind it instead.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: What visual illusion about large trucks causes many car-truck intersection collisions?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Because of their size, tractor-trailers often look slower than they are, and many car-truck crashes at intersections happen when drivers misjudge how close a truck is.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How must you respond to a stopped emergency vehicle flashing red, white, or blue lights, and what infraction applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.memory_hook: Change lanes or drop ten; Class-A
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Approaching an emergency vehicle flashing red, red and white, or red and blue lights, change lanes away from it, or if you cannot, slow to ten miles per hour under the posted limit; failing to comply is a Class A infraction.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: Which five parked amber-light work vehicles get Move Over protection, and what infraction class applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: The same move-over or slow-down rule applies to a parked tow truck, highway maintenance, utility, trash or survey vehicle flashing amber lights, and breaking it is a Class B infraction.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What does Indiana's Move Over rule require when passing a disabled car flashing its hazard lights, and what penalty applies?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.memory_hook: Hazards get lane or ten-under; Class-B
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: For a disabled vehicle with its hazard lights flashing, move over or slow to ten miles per hour under the posted limit, and failing to do so is a Class B infraction.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How does the infraction class differ between failing to move over for emergency red lights versus amber or hazard lights?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: Not moving over for a red-light emergency vehicle is a Class A infraction, while not moving over for an amber-light parked vehicle or a disabled vehicle with hazards is a Class B infraction.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: What does a school bus communicate with flashing amber lights versus flashing red lights and its stop arm?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.memory_hook: Amber warns slowing; red means stopped
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: A school bus flashes amber lights to warn that it is slowing to load or unload children, and turns on red lights and the stop arm once it stops.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: At what stage of a stop do a school bus's amber lights flash compared with its red lights and arm?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.memory_hook: Amber before stopping, red once stopped
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Amber lights on a school bus mean it is about to stop, while red lights with the stop arm come on once it has stopped.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: When must opposite-direction traffic stop for a school bus with red lights and stop arm out, and when may it continue?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: You must stop for a school bus with red lights flashing and its stop arm out, except that on a road divided by a barrier or unimproved median only traffic going the bus's direction must stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What misdemeanor and escalating felony charges can result from ignoring an extended school-bus stop arm?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: Ignoring a school bus stop arm can be a Class A misdemeanor, a Level six felony if someone is hurt, or a Level five felony if someone is killed.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: How much lane width and how many seconds of following distance should you give a motorcycle or motor-driven cycle?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Give motorcycles and motor driven cycles the full width of a lane, and follow them by at least three or four seconds.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: Why should you wait to see a motorcycle actually lean into a turn before pulling out in front of it?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: Motorcycle turn signals usually do not cancel themselves, so wait until the rider actually starts to turn before you proceed.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: What two clearances are required before you may legally overtake a bicyclist?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: You may pass a bicyclist only with at least three feet of space beside the rider and no danger from oncoming traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: How many riders may pedal side by side on a road, and must cyclists stay inside a marked bike lane?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: Bicyclists may ride no more than two abreast except on paths or lanes set aside for bicycles, and they may use either the bike lane or the travel lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How do you avoid cutting off a bicyclist when making a right turn or a left turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: When turning right with a bicyclist coming up on your right, let the cyclist go through first, and when turning left wait for a cyclist coming from the opposite direction to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: What may motorists never do inside a bike lane, and when is crossing one permitted?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.memory_hook: Keep out; cross turning or driveways
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: Do not drive or park in a bike lane, do not move into it to prepare for a turn, and cross it only when turning or entering or leaving an alley, driveway or private road.

sec08-card-sec08-R21.front: After parallel parking, what must you check before swinging your car door open?
sec08-card-sec08-R21.expected_back: After parking, check for bicyclists before you open a car door.

sec08-card-sec08-R22.front: What special users do green-painted pavement and red-painted pavement designate?
sec08-card-sec08-R22.expected_back: Green pavement may mark a bike lane, while red pavement may mark a lane for buses, taxis or other public transit.

sec08-card-sec08-R23.front: What is a sharrow marking, and what two purposes does it serve on a city street?
sec08-card-sec08-R23.expected_back: A sharrow is a pavement marking of a bike with two arrows that helps cyclists stay clear of parked cars and tells drivers to expect cyclists in the lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What legal rights and duties apply to someone riding a horse or driving a buggy on a public road?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: A person riding a horse or driving a horse-drawn vehicle on a public highway has the same rights and duties as a motor vehicle driver.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: Who takes priority when a traffic officer contradicts a signal, and how do official funeral processions cross lights?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: When a police officer directing traffic gives a command that differs from the signal or sign, obey the officer, and official processions such as funerals have the right of way even against a signal.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Which direction should you turn your front tires when parking downhill, uphill with a curb, or without any curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.memory_hook: Up with curb away; else right
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb; facing uphill, turn them away from the curb; with no curb, turn them away from the street.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: How should you position your body to see behind you when backing, and what turnaround move is forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.memory_hook: Turn right, look back; skip intersections
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: To reverse, turn your body to the right and look through the back window rather than relying only on the mirror, and never back into an intersection to turn around.

sec08-card-sec08-R24.front: What setup distance, backing angle, and wheel turn sequence put your car cleanly into a parallel parking spot?
sec08-card-sec08-R24.expected_back: To parallel park, line up beside the car ahead of the space at least two feet away with rear bumpers even, back until you reach a forty-five-degree angle, then turn the wheel left and straighten in the space.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: How close to a fire hydrant is parking banned, along with six other everyday street spots?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Parking is banned within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant, in fire lanes, in intersections or crosswalks, on sidewalks, in front of driveways, beside yellow curbs and next to another parked vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-R25.front: What four highway, structure, or permit-controlled places are also off-limits for parking?
sec08-card-sec08-R25.expected_back: Parking is also prohibited on highways unless allowed, on bridges and in tunnels, and in disability spaces without a valid placard.

sec08-card-sec08-R26.front: Why is the diagonally striped zone next to an accessible parking stall painted, and may placard holders park on it?
sec08-card-sec08-R26.expected_back: The striped area beside an accessible space is kept clear so a wheelchair user can transfer or deploy a vehicle ramp, and parking there is banned even with a valid placard.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: To which pedestrians must motorists always yield, and what two mobility aids help you recognize them?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.memory_hook: White cane or guide dog yields
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Drivers must always yield to a visually impaired pedestrian, who is often traveling with a white cane or a guide dog.

sec08-card-sec08-R27.front: What effect on a crossing pedestrian makes a driver's turn improper?
sec08-card-sec08-R27.expected_back: Never make a turn that forces a pedestrian to stop, slow down or take special effort to avoid you.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: Who must buckle up inside a moving vehicle in Indiana, and do air bags replace seat belts?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Indiana law requires the driver and every passenger to wear a seat belt whenever the vehicle is moving, even in a car with air bags.

sec08-card-sec08-R28.front: Where should lap and shoulder straps rest on your body, and how far back from the wheel should you sit?
sec08-card-sec08-R28.expected_back: Wear the seat belt low on the hips and flat across the collarbone, and sit at least twelve inches from the steering wheel.

sec08-card-sec08-R29.front: By what percentages do front-seat belts boost crash survival and reduce serious injury risk?
sec08-card-sec08-R29.expected_back: Belts worn by the driver and front-seat passenger raise the chance of surviving a crash by forty-five percent and cut serious injury risk by fifty percent.

sec08-card-sec08-R30.front: What proof must someone carry to be legally excused from wearing a seat belt for medical reasons?
sec08-card-sec08-R30.expected_back: A person excused from a seat belt for medical reasons needs written documentation from a physician.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: Up to what age must Indiana passengers ride secured in a car seat or booster seat?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Passengers younger than eight must be secured in a child restraint system such as a car seat or booster seat.

sec08-card-sec08-R31.front: In vehicles with a passenger-side air bag, under what age does the National Safety Council advise seating kids in back?
sec08-card-sec08-R31.expected_back: Where there is a passenger-side air bag, the National Safety Council advises seating children younger than twelve in the back seat.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Where must three warning lights or reflectors sit around a disabled passenger car at night on a divided highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.memory_hook: Hundred ahead, hundred back, ten side
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: When headlights are needed on a divided highway, a disabled car must have a lighted fuse, red lantern or red reflector placed one hundred feet behind and one hundred feet ahead in the center of its lane, plus one about ten feet away on the traffic side.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Which three emergency warning kits satisfy the breakdown rule for a disabled truck, bus, or tractor-trailer?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.memory_hook: Three triangles, six fuses, three flares
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: A disabled truck, bus or tractor-trailer must put out three bi-directional reflective triangles, or at least six fuses or three liquid-burning flares, unlike the fuse, lantern or reflector set used for a car.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How is a disabled car marked in daylight, and how far out must markers move near a curve or hilltop?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: In daylight a disabled car shows two red flags about one hundred feet ahead and one hundred feet behind, and within five hundred feet of a curve or hilltop a warning device must sit at least five hundred feet away.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: On a divided highway, how far out does a disabled truck place its warning device compared with a car?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: For a disabled truck, the warning device goes two hundred feet away on a divided highway instead of about one hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-R32.front: When cargo or a tailgate extends past four feet behind a vehicle, how must you mark it day and night?
sec08-card-sec08-R32.memory_hook: Over four feet, flag or lamp
sec08-card-sec08-R32.expected_back: A load or tailgate sticking out more than four feet past the rear needs a red lamp visible from five hundred feet at night and a red flag of at least twelve square inches by day.

sec08-card-sec08-R33.front: What lights should you activate whenever your vehicle breaks down, even after pulling clear onto the shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-R33.expected_back: If your car breaks down, turn on its hazard lights if it has them, even when you have pulled onto the shoulder.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: Which four proof categories — and how many Indiana residency papers — must a first-time applicant bring in original or certified form?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: A first-time applicant for a license, learner's permit or ID card must bring originals or verifiable certified copies proving identity, lawful status in the US and full Social Security number, plus two documents proving Indiana residency.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: What must someone renewing, amending, or replacing a current Indiana card bring to upgrade to a Real ID?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Someone renewing, amending or replacing a current Indiana credential should bring original or certified documents to a branch if they want a Real ID-compliant credential.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Which U.S. birth certificates prove identity at the BMV — and which keepsake hospital version gets rejected?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: A US birth certificate used as identity proof must be an original or certified copy issued by a government agency, and unofficial hospital birth certificates are not accepted.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: Under what condition can a U.S. passport book or passport card prove your identity?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: A US passport or passport card can prove identity only if it is not expired.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: What three items must accompany a foreign passport for it to prove identity at an Indiana branch?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: A foreign passport proves identity only when it is unexpired and carries a US visa with an approved I-ninety-four form showing the most recent admission or current status.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What two conditions let a Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card prove identity?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: A Permanent Resident Card or Employment Authorization Card can prove identity only if it is unexpired and its lawful status has been verified.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: For someone born outside the U.S., which requirement can a delayed birth certificate satisfy — and which can't it?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: A person born outside the US may use a delayed birth certificate to prove identity, but not lawful status.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: If an applicant born abroad brings a delayed birth certificate for identity, how do they handle lawful status?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: A delayed birth certificate for someone born abroad works for identity, while lawful status must be shown another way.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: What two official steps validate an amended birth certificate showing a changed legal name or birth date?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: An amended birth certificate showing a new legal name or date of birth must be certified and filed with the vital statistics office in the state of birth.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Once a non-citizen earns a Real ID Indiana credential, how can that card help in later BMV visits?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: A non-citizen who received a Real ID-compliant credential using one of the listed documents may use that credential as identity proof in later transactions.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: If your current legal name or birth date differs from your birth certificate, what linking proof must you bring?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: If your legal name or date of birth differs from your identity documents, you must show legal proof of the change, such as a marriage license, divorce decree or court order.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: For a U.S. citizen, how many documents are needed to cover both identity and lawful status?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: For a US citizen, the document used to prove identity also proves lawful status.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: What two conditions make a federal Notice of Action acceptable as proof of lawful status?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: A Notice of Action form proves lawful status only if the BMV verifies that DHS received it without denying action and the applicant also submits pertaining federal-agency documents showing lawful status.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: When does proof of an asylum application count toward Indiana's lawful-status requirement?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Proof of an asylum application verified by DHS is listed as a lawful status document.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Which four everyday tax or payroll documents — showing your name and full nine digits — prove your Social Security number?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: A Social Security number can be proven with a document showing your name and full number, such as a Social Security card, a W-two, a one thousand ninety-nine or a pre-printed pay stub.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What must an applicant not authorized to work in the U.S. submit instead of a Social Security number?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: An applicant not authorized to work in the US who does not qualify for a Social Security number must submit documents showing that, and may be asked for a valid I-ninety-four instead.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: Who is the ONLY group allowed to list a P.O. box as their residential address on an Indiana credential?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Only applicants in the Indiana Attorney General's Address Confidentiality Program may list a post office box as their residential address.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: Within how many days of applying must utility bills, medical bills, bank statements, or pay stubs be dated?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A utility, credit card, doctor or hospital bill, a bank statement or a pre-printed pay stub can prove residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within sixty days of applying.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: How recent must a homeowner's, renter's, or auto insurance policy be to prove Indiana residency?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: A homeowner's, renter's or vehicle insurance policy proves residency if it shows your name and residential address and is dated within one year of applying.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: Contrast the acceptable date window for W-twos, tax bills, and benefits statements against insurance policies?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: A W-two, property or excise tax bill, or benefits statement must be dated in the current or prior year, whereas an insurance policy must be dated within one year of the application.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: Which civic registration card and student enrollment records count as Indiana residency documents?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: An Indiana voter registration card and public or private school records showing an enrolled student's name and residential address are among the accepted residency documents.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: What two addresses must appear on a U.S. Postal Service change-of-address confirmation to prove residency?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: A US Postal Service change of address confirmation showing both prior and current address can prove residency.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Which four living situations allow filing an Indiana Residency Affidavit when you lack two address documents?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: An applicant without two residency documents may file an Indiana Residency Affidavit if they are incapacitated, homeless, living with a relative or friend, or living in a motor vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: When you live with a relative or friend, what age and documents must your host bring to co-sign at the branch?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: For an applicant living with a relative or friend, that person, aged at least eighteen, signs the affidavit at a branch and shows their own Indiana credential, identity proof and two Indiana address documents.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: Contrast who signs the Indiana Residency Affidavit for an incapacitated applicant versus a homeless applicant?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: For an incapacitated applicant the affidavit is signed by a resident guardian or caregiver aged at least eighteen, while for a homeless applicant it is signed by a representative of the agency or nonprofit that serves them.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What signer and three Indiana records must someone living in a motor home bring for a Residency Affidavit?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: An applicant living in a motor vehicle such as a motor home needs another Indiana resident to sign the affidavit at a branch and must show Indiana income tax payment plus current title and registration records with the BMV.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Which document formats does the BMV accept — and what four red flags trigger rejection at the counter?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: The BMV accepts only original documents or certified copies from the issuing agency and may refuse any document that looks fraudulent, unreliable, altered or expired.
